desc: Prove the pairwise-conflict conjecture via exhaustive verification on small cases (brute-force feasibility via Bellman-Ford on the difference-constraint system with strict edges as >=1/<=-1, enumerate all subsets of candidate people for small N, compare with pairwise condition); if a counterexample exists, derive the correct multi-person witness structure.

Design an efficient, Python-feasible algorithm for gL(j) = max i<j conflicting with j: (1) same-left/right-endpoint conflicts via last-occurrence arrays O(1) per person; (2) same-type crossing conflicts as a 3D offline problem (i<j, c_i<a_j, d_i in (a_j,b_j), and symmetric case) — settle on CDQ O(M log² M) with heavy optimization vs a smarter O(M log M) sweep; specify exact structures and event orders.

Implement the full verified solution in Python: normalization; shared-endpoint pass; two CDQ runs (per type) with iterative max segment tree over compressed d handling shapes α and β; sparse table over gL; query answering (No iff max(gL[L..R]) >= L); fast I/O.

Fix the critical type-mixing bug in the CDQ (issue #5): replace the single shared segment tree with two trees (one per type) — insert every left-half interval into seg[Tp[i]], query seg[tj], and reset each tree's own touched list. Then actually run the stress tests: gL vs O(M²) reference on random small inputs, full pipeline vs Bellman-Ford feasibility, adversarial families, and both samples; fix any failures found.

Complexity/constant optimization pass for N,M,Q up to 4e5/2e5/2e5: carry sorted orders through CDQ via merges instead of per-node `sorted`, replace seg_reset set/sort with stack-based parent recompute, tune LEAF cutoff (~48), PyPy-compatible hot loops; performance-test at max constraints (dense-crossing worst case).
